Mikołaj Firlej (1588–1635) was a prominent Polish nobleman and military commander during the early 17th century, a period of significant political and military upheaval in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth.

## Family Background
Firlej came from the influential Firlej family, one of the notable noble houses in Poland. He was the son of Jan Firlej and belonged to a family that had produced several important political and military figures in Polish history.

## Political Career
- He served as a senator in the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
- Held the position of voivode (governor) of Sandomierz Voivodeship
- Was active in the Polish Sejm (parliament) and participated in the political life of the Commonwealth

## Military Service
Firlej was particularly distinguished as a military commander:
- He participated in various military campaigns during the troubled times of the early 17th century
- Served during the period of the Swedish invasions and other conflicts that plagued the Commonwealth
- Was known for his loyalty to the Polish crown and his military competence

## Historical Context
His life spanned a particularly turbulent period in Polish history, including:
- The Time of Troubles in neighboring Russia
- Various Swedish interventions in Polish affairs
- Internal political struggles within the Commonwealth
- The ongoing conflicts with the Ottoman Empire

## Legacy
Firlej represents the type of noble military commander who was crucial to the Commonwealth's defense during this challenging period. His family's continued prominence in Polish politics and military affairs helped maintain stability in the Sandomierz region.

The historical records about him, while not as extensive as those of some of his contemporaries, indicate he was a reliable servant of the Commonwealth who fulfilled his duties both as a regional administrator and military leader during a critical period in Polish history.
